source_spans.locator: Nature Reviews Neuroscience 11, published pp.127-128 / author PDF pp.1-2, opening motivation and Box 1: adaptive biological agents occupy a limited repertoire of states; long-run average surprise is minimized; variational free energy is an evaluable upper bound on surprise

Nature Reviews Neuroscience 11, published pp.128-129 / author PDF pp.2-3, Box 1 and Implications: free energy depends on sensory samples, a recognition density encoded by internal states, and a generative model; internal-state optimization changes the recognition density whereas action changes sampled sensory input

Nature Reviews Neuroscience 11, published pp.133-135 / author PDF pp.7-9, Neural Darwinism and value learning plus Optimal control theory: prior expectations specify valuable/attracting states and motion; under the stated optimal-policy assumption value is inversely related to surprise, free energy bounds expected cost, and rewards/goals can be encoded as priors fulfilled by action

institutions: The Wellcome Trust Centre for Neuroimaging, University College London

conditions: the source's optimization formulation is applied to an adaptive biological agent whose characteristic physiological and sensory states occupy a limited repertoire
the agent is modeled as having a joint probability density over sensory samples and hidden causes plus a recognition density encoded by internal states

the value/control identification is conditional on the source's stated assumption that an optimal policy performs gradient ascent on value; priors over states or their motion may be learned or innate and can encode goals, rewards, or costs
population: adaptive biological agents, including animals or brains in the source's framing
substrate: sensory and hidden environmental states, internal states, actions, and probabilistic generative and recognition densities
task: minimize an agent-accessible bound objective through perceptual/internal-state optimization and action while realizing state trajectories specified by prior expectations
temporal_scope: short-term minimization of the accessible bound objective is related to long-run average surprise, while the value/control discussion concerns expected future states and priors over motion through state space

nodes.description: sensory states sampled through the agent's exchange with the environment
joint probability density over sensory samples and their hidden causes, including prior densities
probabilistic representation of sensory causes encoded by the agent's internal states
agent-accessible information-theoretic objective that upper-bounds sensory surprise and, in the source's control-theoretic comparison, expected cost
value as expected reward or utility, or its complementary expected loss or cost over future states under a policy
prior expectations over states or motion through state space that can specify valuable attractors, rewards, goals, or costs
source-explicit optimization of internal states that changes the recognition density toward the conditional density on sensory causes
action on the environment that changes which sensory states are sampled
trajectory through sensory or hidden state space realized through action under the agent's prior expectations

relations.description: the accessible bound objective is defined from sensory input, the recognition density, and the joint probability density over sensations and their hidden causes
optimizing internal states changes the recognition density toward the conditional density and reduces the accessible bound objective without directly changing current sensory samples
action changes sampled sensory input so as to increase prediction accuracy and thereby reduce the accessible bound objective
prior expectations can encode rewards, goals, and cost functions and thereby specify which states or trajectories count as valuable or costly
under the stated gradient-ascent-on-value assumption, value is inversely proportional to surprise and the accessible bound objective is an upper bound on expected cost
priors over states or their motion prescribe attracting trajectories or policies that action tends to fulfil by changing sensory sampling
